data.body_html:
September in Marbella is often called the ‘secret summer’ — the heat of July and August mellows, the sea stays warm, and the Mediterranean settles into a calm rhythm. If you’re planning a marbella boat rental weather september trip, you’ve picked the sweet spot. Air temperatures sit at 25-30°C, sea water is 22-24°C, and you get 7-8 hours of daily sunshine. The crowds thin, the moorings in Puerto Banús ease up, and the light Poniente wind (5-15 knots) keeps the sea gentle. This guide breaks down everything you need to know: temperatures, wind, sea conditions, sunset times, and which boat from our fleet suits your September plans. All our charters depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance — so you just show up and enjoy.

September Air Temperatures in Marbella

Daytime highs in September average 30°C, with lows around 20°C at night. The humidity drops compared to August, making it feel more comfortable. By the sea, a light breeze often keeps the heat in check. If you’re on the water between 11:00 and 16:00, expect full sun and temperatures in the high 20s. Evenings cool quickly after sunset (around 20:30), so bring a light jacket if you plan a sunset cruise. Compared to July (which can hit 35°C+), September is noticeably milder — perfect for long hours on deck without overheating.

Sea Temperature and Swimming Conditions

The Mediterranean off Marbella in September is 22-24°C — warm enough for extended swimming, snorkelling, or paddleboarding without a wetsuit. The water stays this warm through mid-October. Our favourite swimming spots include Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, both sheltered coves with clear water. If you’re on a boat rental in Marbella, your skipper will know the calmest anchorages. The sea is typically clearest in the morning before the afternoon breeze stirs up sediment.

Wind and Sea State in September

September’s prevailing wind is the Poniente (westerly), blowing 5-15 knots — ideal for a smooth ride. Mornings are often glassy (0.3-0.6 m swell), with a gentle sea breeze building after lunch. The Levante (easterly) is less frequent but can bring stronger gusts (15-25 knots) and a choppier sea, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. On such days, your skipper will adjust the route to stay in sheltered waters. For context, our Mangusta 80 (24m) handles rougher seas with ease, while smaller boats like the Dubhe (8m) are best kept in calm conditions — which is most of September.

Sunshine Hours and UV Index

September delivers 7-8 hours of direct sunshine daily, with sunrise around 07:30 and sunset at 20:30. The UV index is 6-7 (high), so sunscreen (SPF 30+), a hat, and sunglasses are non-negotiable. The sun’s angle is lower than in July, but you’ll still burn quickly if you’re not careful. Reapply after swimming. The golden hour from 19:00 to 20:30 is spectacular — the light over La Concha mountain and the Marbella coastline is perfect for photos.

Rainfall and Humidity

September is one of the driest months in Marbella, with only 15-20 mm of precipitation — typically a brief afternoon shower that passes within 30 minutes. Humidity averages 60-70%, lower than August’s 75-80%. You can expect at least 25 completely dry days. If you’re checking the forecast 48 hours before your charter, any rain is unlikely to affect your plans. Our boats have covered cockpits and saloons, so a short shower won’t spoil the day.

Best Boats for September Charters

All our boats are available in September, but some suit the conditions particularly well. For a couple or small group, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are nimble and easy to dock. For families or groups of 8-10, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax, €749/2h) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax, €749/2h) offer excellent value with a flybridge for sunbathing. If you want luxury, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, €4,719 minimum 4h) includes a free jet ski — perfect for exploring the coast between Puerto Banús and Cabopino. Every charter includes a skipper, fuel, soft drinks, beer, wine, cava, snacks, and Spanish VAT.

September Itinerary Suggestions

With calm seas and long daylight, you have several route options. A 4-hour charter can take you from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro for a swim, then past the Golden Mile to Marbella Marina. An 8-hour charter lets you reach Estepona (12 NM west) or Cabopino (8 NM east) for lunch at a chiringuito. For a full-day adventure, head to Sotogrande (25 NM) — the sea is usually flat enough in September. Sunset cruises from 18:00 to 20:30 are also popular, with the sun setting behind La Concha.

What to Wear and Pack for a September Boat Trip

Pack swimwear, a T-shirt, shorts, a light jacket or windbreaker, sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses. Non-slip shoes are a good idea on deck. The water is warm enough for swimming without a wetsuit. If you plan to use the jet ski on the Mangusta 80, bring a change of clothes. Our boats have coolers with ice, so you can bring extra drinks if you wish — though we already provide soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava.
